lines.text: Let's take a closer look at the Nexon.
We'll explore its safety equipment, cabin and luggage space. You can pause or ask about another detail at any point.
The brochure lists the Nexon's length as 3,995 millimetres. Exterior dimensions alone don't establish passenger comfort.
Tata reports five-star Global NCAP and Bharat NCAP ratings. Its Bharat NCAP scope covers petrol and diesel trims active in May 2026.
Keep three areas in mind: standard safety equipment, boot space by fuel type, and cabin features by trim.
I'm happy to stay with the part that interests you.
Six airbags and electronic stability control are standard equipment.
For ground clearance, Tata lists 208 millimetres, with variation by variant.
Notice the side profile.
Tata lists 208 millimetres of ground clearance, which varies by variant. It isn't a promise about water depth or clearing every obstacle.
Smart and Pure use 195/60 R16 tyres; Creative and Fearless use 215/60 R16.
The brochure lists front disc and rear drum brakes.
Here is the centre touchscreen.
Pure plus begins with the 26.03-centimetre Harman touchscreen; Fearless plus P S adds a matching-size driver display.
The 26.03-centimetre Harman touchscreen starts at Pure plus in this brochure's trim list.
The larger driver display is listed on Fearless plus P S. Check the exact trim when comparing cabins.
Here is the luggage area.
Petrol and diesel list 382 litres; CNG lists 321, both measured to ISO V215. Your bags still deserve a physical fit check.
Both boot figures use ISO V215. A number alone cannot tell us whether your stroller will fit.
The petrol fuel tank is listed at 44 litres. We don't have a verified real-world range figure here.
Nexon has petrol, diesel and CNG choices, with different gearbox options.
If you prefer an automatic, petrol options include a seven-speed dual-clutch gearbox. Availability depends on the trim.
The 1.2-litre turbo petrol is listed at 88.2 kilowatts at 5,500 rpm in the brochure.
The 1.5-litre turbo diesel is listed at 84.5 kilowatts at 3,750 rpm, with 260 newton-metres at 1,500 to 2,750 rpm.
Tata reports a five-star Bharat NCAP rating for petrol and diesel trims active in May 2026.
Six airbags and electronic stability control are standard.
Tata lists three-point emergency-locking seatbelts for all occupants.
ADAS, including autonomous emergency braking and lane keep assist, is listed only for Fearless plus P S petrol DCA.
Here are a few details worth comparing by trim.
Creative adds a 360-degree camera with blind-view monitor; JBL audio with a subwoofer is limited to Fearless plus P S petrol DCA.
Fearless plus P S petrol and diesel list iRA connectivity. The first year is free; renewal charges apply.
Driver-assistance features are limited to Fearless plus P S petrol DCA. CNG and diesel aren't listed with them.
Prices start at seven point three nine lakh rupees ex-showroom, subject to change.
Your chosen trim and on-road quote need a dealer check; finance depends on the lender.
The advertised starting EMI is six thousand four hundred and ninety-nine rupees. It covers a Flexi scheme's first six months; later instalments are higher, and the financier decides approval.
Tata publishes a roadside-assistance contact. The supplied footer doesn't specify the helpline's opening hours.
The Nexon brings standard safety equipment, distinct fuel choices and cabin upgrades to compare by trim.
Choose Book Test Drive when you're ready to try the seats, visibility and gearbox for yourself.
